title: Serbia's Vucic Concedes Defeat to Student-Led Movement
paragraphs: Aleksandar Vucic, who has dominated Serbian politics for well over a decade, has conceded defeat in a parliamentary election to a movement that grew out of student-led protests.

The snap election was held on Sunday, October 25. About an hour and a half after polls closed, Vucic appeared before supporters at his party's election-night event and acknowledged that the opposition "Students' List" had won. He projected that the movement would take between 135 and 140 seats in Serbia's 250-seat parliament, compared with about 105 for his Serbian Progressive Party (SNS), which had held power for 14 years. Monitors had predicted turnout of around 70 percent, which would be the highest since 2000.

The movement's origins lie in a tragedy. In November 2024, a concrete canopy collapsed at a railway station in the northern city of Novi Sad, killing 16 people. The disaster sparked nearly two years of youth-led protests, with demonstrators blaming corruption and cronyism linked to the station's renovation. Critics also accused the government of dismantling democratic institutions, and monitors raised concerns about near-total government control of the media and the surveillance of activists.

Unusually, although the movement was shaped by university students, none of them actually appeared on its list of candidates. Instead, it put forward little-known experts, athletes, farmers and artists. The movement campaigned on a non-partisan platform of economic recovery and restoring democracy, and it managed to win support even in rural areas that had traditionally been Vucic strongholds.

Vucic, who had resigned from the presidency the previous month in order to lead his party's campaign and seek the post of prime minister, blamed his defeat on independent media, alleged interference by unnamed European countries and what he called an "American deep state."

Celebrations broke out in Belgrade and other cities as the results became clear. Dijana Hrka, whose son was among those killed in the Novi Sad disaster, said she had been waiting two years for this moment and expected everyone responsible to be held accountable.
The result is being closely watched by the European Union, since Serbia is a candidate for EU membership. Russian President Vladimir Putin had endorsed Vucic ahead of the vote.
